ApiKeyHelp: Routarr generates one at first start unless ROUTARR_API_KEY is set. Scripts send it as X-Api-Key. This browser sent it once to open a session, and keeps no copy.
ApiKeyHelpSession: Sign-in uses your session. This key is for clients that cannot hold one, such as scripts and monitoring, which send it as X-Api-Key.
ApiKeyKeepHint: Leave blank to keep the current key
ApiKeyMintedOnce: Copy it now. It is shown once and cannot be read again.
ApiKeyPinned: ROUTARR_API_KEY sets this key, so it cannot be changed here.
ApplicationsSubtitle: Keys for the applications that call Routarr on their own, such as a script, n8n or Home Assistant. Each key reaches only what you allow it.
ApplicationMayConfirmHelp: A question it may not answer is left to a person in Routarr. Only a key that operates is ever asked.
ApiReferenceSubtitle: The operations another application may call, with the scope each needs, as this version describes them.
ApiReferenceEnglish: The descriptions are written in English, like the API they describe.
ApiReferenceKeys: Each call sends a key made on the {screen} screen, in its X-Api-Key header.
ApiDeprecatedNote: Renamed paths, still answered under their old name until a release before 1.0 removes them. Every answer carries a Deprecation header. Call the new path instead.
GuardrailCapacity: Not enough room at the destination
GuardrailThreshold: More moves than the confirmation threshold
NoApplications: No application has a key yet.
ScopeOperateHelp: Sync, simulate, apply, revert, run the rule tests and take a backup.
ScopeReadHelp: Everything the screens show, except the settings, the keys and the backup archives. Every key reads.
ScopeWriteHelp: Add or remove an exception, which forces a title's category.
ScopeConfigureHelp: Create, change or remove rules, categories, folder mappings, declared destinations and rule tests: what decides where every title goes.
ApiKeyMissingHint: No API key is stored. Edit the instance to enter it.
ApiKeyRejected: That key was refused. Check it and try again.
ApiKeyRequired: This Routarr needs an API key
ApiKeyChooseOwn: To choose the key yourself instead, set {variable} and restart Routarr.
ProofPasswordHelp: A key outlives the session that makes it. Type the current password to go on.
ProofKeyHelp: A key outlives the session that makes it. Type the current API key to go on.
ProofPasswordArchiveHelp: An archive carries the master key and the API key. Type the current password to download it.
ProofKeyArchiveHelp: An archive carries the master key and the API key. Type the current API key to download it.
ErrorPassphraseNeeded: This archive is encrypted. Give the passphrase it was taken with.
ErrorPassphraseWrong: That passphrase does not open this archive.
ErrorPassphraseShort: A backup passphrase needs at least {min} characters.
JobDetailResealing: Converting the archives to the backup passphrase
JobDetailResealed: Archives converted: {archives}. Left as they were: {left}
JobDetailBackupCopyBusy: The copy before this one to {folder} has not ended, and nothing was copied. A share that hangs holds it.
JobDetailBackupCopyMissing: {folder} is no folder Routarr can reach, and nothing was copied. Check that it is mounted into the container.
JobDetailBackupCopyUnmounted: {folder} lacks the file its first copy left there, so the share may not be mounted, and nothing was copied. If the folder was changed on purpose, start the copy there from the Backups card, on the Maintenance tab of Settings.
JobDetailBackupCopyForeign: {folder} holds the archives another Routarr database copied there, so nothing was copied or removed. Restore one of them with routarr restore, or start the copy there from the Backups card, on the Maintenance tab of Settings, to take the folder as it is.
JobDetailBackupCopyTimedOut: The copy to {folder} did not end in time. If the share answers late, the copy still ends, and the next one confirms it.
JobDetailBackupCopyFailed: The backups could not be copied to {folder}: {reason}
BackupCopyStarted: The folder is taken as it is. The copy runs now.
BackupCopySameDisk: This folder sits on the disk that holds the database, so losing that disk loses the copies too. Mount a folder from another disk or a NAS to keep them apart.
ConfirmBackupCopyStart: Copy into {folder} as it is now? Do it only for a folder changed on purpose: into a share that is not mounted, the copies would fill the local disk.
ConfirmBackupCopyForeign: Copy into {folder} as it is now? The archives another Routarr database left there stay as they are, and only the copies this database makes are pruned.
BackupEncryptionHelp: Every archive carries the master key, which opens every credential Routarr stores. With a passphrase, a copy of the backups folder opens nothing without it.
BackupPassphraseKeep: Keep the passphrase somewhere else, as a password manager would: a restore on another server asks for it, and nothing opens an archive without it.
ConfirmStopEncrypting: Stop encrypting the archives? Every archive on disk is opened and kept in the clear, master key included.
PassphraseSaved: Passphrase saved. The archives on disk are being converted, see Tasks.
EncryptionStopped: Encryption stopped. The archives on disk are being opened, see Tasks.
ProofPassphraseHelp: This archive is encrypted. Type the passphrase it was taken with.
SignInAgainHelp: Sign in again at your provider first: making or removing a key needs a sign-in from the last ten minutes.
AccountHelp: The password of the account this Routarr signs in. Changing it ends every other session.
RevokeEveryKeyHelp: Every application key stops working, and the API key is replaced: the new one is shown once. For a password that leaked.
PasswordChanged: Password changed. Every other session was ended.
PasswordChangedKeysRevoked: Password changed. Every other session was ended and every key revoked.
SessionsHelp: Each browser signed in, and when. A session ends on its own after 30 days, or 24 hours through an OpenID Connect provider.
ReadOnlyHelp: You can read everything here and change nothing. Whoever runs Routarr can let you do more.
ConfirmEndSession: End this session? The browser holding it will have to sign in again.
ConfirmEndThisSession: End the session of this browser? You will have to sign in again.
ConfirmEndEverySession: End every session, this one included? Every browser will have to sign in again.
ApiKeyDockerCommand: With the Docker image, this command prints it:
ApiKeyGeneratedFile: Routarr generated it at first start and saved it as {file} next to the database. This browser sends it once to open a session, and keeps no copy.
ApplyAllHint: Applies every move this run proposed, including those beyond the displayed list, in batches.
ApplyMatchingHint: Applies every move of this run the filters keep, including those beyond this page, in batches.
SelectionCapped: The selection stops at the batch limit. Moves at a time: {limit}.
ApplyResultWithSkipped: Decisions applied: {applied} of {requested}, no longer actionable: {skipped}.
ArrHandshakeFailed: The secure connection to {address} failed. If the port serves plain HTTP, write the address with http://. Otherwise the certificate of {service} is not one Routarr trusts.
ArrKeyRefused: {service} refused the API key. Copy it again from {service}: Settings → General → Security → API Key.
ArrMetadataAddress: A cloud host's metadata service answers at {address}, and no {service} does. Routarr does not connect there: use the address of the machine or the container running {service}.
ArrNameUnresolved: The name in {address} does not resolve. Check its spelling. In Docker, a container name resolves only when Routarr and {service} share a network.
ArrNotHttp: {address} does not answer in HTTP. If the port serves HTTPS, write the address with https://. Otherwise check the port.
ArrNotTheApi: Something answers at {address}, but not {service}'s API. Check the port, and add the URL base if {service} has one, for example {base}.
ArrProxyRefused: The request was refused before it reached {service} (HTTP 403). A proxy, a firewall rule or a sign-in policy in front of it is the likely cause.
ArrProxySignIn: Something in front of {service} asks for its own sign-in. Give Routarr an address that reaches {service} without it.
ArrProxyUnreachable: The address answers, but {service} behind it does not (HTTP {status}). Check that {service} is running, or wait until it has started.
ArrRedirectLoop: {address} redirects to itself without end. Check the URL base, and the rules of any proxy in front of {service}.
ArrRedirected: {address} redirects to another address, where Routarr does not send the API key. Enter the address it redirects to, often with https:// or a URL base.
ArrRedirectedElsewhere: {address} redirects to {host}. If {service} answers there, enter that address. If it is a sign-in page, give Routarr an address that reaches {service} without it.
ArrServerError: {service} failed on its own side (HTTP {status}). Its log says why, under System → Logs in {service}.
ArrTimedOut: {service} did not answer in time at {address}. Check the address, and that no firewall drops the connection.
ArrUnreachable: Nothing answers at {address}. Check that {service} is running, and the address and the port.
ArrUnreachableLoopback: Nothing answers at {address}. If Routarr runs in Docker, localhost is Routarr's own container: use {service}'s container name or the host's IP address instead.
ArrWrongApp: {address} answers as {found}, not {service}. Change the type, or the port: Radarr usually listens on 7878 and Sonarr on 8989.

AuditProofRefused: A session asked to make or remove a key without its proof.

AuditInstanceCredentialChanged: The address or the API key of {instance} was changed.

For a copy off this machine, download an archive under Backups, or copy the backups folder beside the database. A copy of routarr.db taken while Routarr runs can miss every recent change.
BackupsHelp: Taken on a schedule and kept beside the database. Each archive holds the database, the master key and the API key, everything a restore needs, which makes the file as sensitive as the key itself.
BatchApplyStopped: Stopped after a failure. Applied: {applied} of {candidates}. Batches run: {run} of {planned}. The rest is still pending.
BatchRevertStopped: Stopped after a failure. Reverted: {applied} of {candidates}. Batches run: {run} of {planned}. The rest stays applied.

ConfirmDeleteOverride: Remove the exception on "{title}"? The rules take over again.

ConfirmRemoveKey: Remove the API key? Clients using it stop working immediately.
ConfirmRemoveDestination: Remove the destination {path}? A category mapped to it no longer routes there. Nothing is deleted on disk.

GuideCategoriesText: A category names where a kind of title belongs, such as anime or kids. Give each root folder the Arr reports a category, starting with the default one. When a folder's name says its category, the screen suggests it.
GuideComplete: Routarr is set up. Apply the moves you agree with from the simulation, whenever you are ready.
GuideInstanceText: Routarr reads your library through the Arr's own API. Add an instance with its address and API key, and Routarr syncs it at once.
GuideIntro: A few steps take Routarr from a fresh install to its first proposed moves. Each one ticks itself once it is done, so you can leave and come back at any time.
GuideLiveText: While the global dry-run is on, no move reaches Radarr or Sonarr. Turn it off once the decisions look right.
GuideMetadataText: Radarr and Sonarr already supply genres, language and certification. TMDB, AniList and the other sources add keywords and countries.
GuidePaused: The setup is not finished. Required steps done: {done} of {total}
GuidePillLabel: Getting started, required steps done: {done} of {total}
GuideRestartText: Show the getting-started steps on the dashboard again.
GuideRuleText: Start from a template, a ready-made rule set for a common library split, or write your own rules. Rules run by priority, and the first that matches wins.
GuideSimulationText: A simulation proposes where each title belongs and says why. Nothing is written to Radarr or Sonarr.
GuideOptionalNext: Step {number} of {total} is done. Next, optional: {next}
GuideUnavailable: The getting-started guide could not be read: {error}
HelpCardAccount: On the Security tab when Routarr signs in with a password. Change the password, at least 12 characters, and every other session ends. Tick Also revoke every key when the password leaked: every application key stops and the API key is replaced.
HelpCardApiSchemas: Every type the operations take or return, by name. Open one to read its fields, their types, whether each is required and what it holds, when a request body or a response names it.
HelpCardApiDeprecated: The old names of the renamed paths. Each still answers what its new path does, with the same scope, and says it is deprecated in a Deprecation header. A release before 1.0 removes them, so a script calls the new path.
HelpCardApiTagBackups: The backups kept, and taking one on request. Taking one needs Operate, and an application key may take one at most every ten minutes.
HelpCardApiTagCategories: The categories, the root folders of each Arr and the category each folder leads to, with what the mappings leave unsaid. Creating, renaming or removing a category, declaring a destination the Arr does not list and mapping a folder all need Configure.
HelpCardApiTagDecisions: Running a simulation, listing the decisions it stored, and applying or reverting their moves behind the same guardrails as the interface. Every operation but the list needs Operate, and moving files needs a key allowed to. A 409 answer names the guardrail that asks in its confirm field.
HelpCardApiTagExceptions: Exceptions force a title's category and outrank every rule. Listing them only reads, and adding or removing one needs Write. The external operations name the title by its TMDB, TheTVDB or IMDb id, for an application that does not know Routarr's own ids.
HelpCardApiTagInstances: The Radarr and Sonarr instances Routarr reads, one or all, and reading them again. A sync needs Operate and answers one report per instance, and an instance that fails stops none of the others. Adding or editing an instance stays on the Instances screen.
HelpCardApiTagLibrary: The titles Routarr read from the Arrs, a page at a time or one by one, and where each one goes and why. /route answers where a title another service names would go, even one the library does not hold, and stores nothing. Every operation here only reads.
HelpCardApiTagRules: The rules in priority order, the conditions they may use, what each rule decides, and the rule tests. Changing a rule or a rule test, and judging a draft rule with validate or preview, needs Configure. Running the rule tests needs Operate, and the rest only reads.
HelpCardApiTagStatus: Whether Routarr is up and what needs attention. /ping needs no key and suits an uptime monitor, /status answers the counts and warnings without reaching anything, and /health checks every Arr and source, which needs Operate. It also holds the Prometheus metrics, the metadata sources and who a key belongs to.
HelpCardApiTagTasks: The tasks that ran in the background, how each ended and what it reported, and the move log with its CSV export. A long call sent with Prefer: respond-async answers with a task id, and that task's result holds the report once it has finished. Everything here only reads.
HelpCardArrInstances: Each Radarr and Sonarr instance as the check found it: whether it answers, the version it runs, how many titles Routarr holds from it, how many of its root folders are mapped and when it was last synced. An Error status carries its reason beside it, and zero mapped folders means its titles go nowhere.
HelpCardBackupEncryption: On the Maintenance tab, the passphrase every backup archive is sealed with, typed twice. The badge says whether archives are encrypted. Keep the passphrase elsewhere: a restore on another server asks for it.
HelpCardBackups: On the Maintenance tab, the archives kept beside the database, with their date and size. Back up now takes one, and each can be downloaded, restored or deleted. A restore replaces the database and the master key at the next restart.
HelpCardCapacityTitle: Each root folder this run would move titles into, with the number of titles, the data arriving and the free space its Arr reports. A free figure too small for what is arriving is flagged, and a warning above names that folder. Data moving within the same volume is shown apart, since it takes no extra room.
HelpCardCategories: Every category with its description, the rules using it and the folders mapped to it. Rename one with the pencil, and rules, folder mappings, exceptions and the decision history follow the new name. A category still in use cannot be deleted, and the default one has no delete button.
HelpCardDashboardInstances: Each Radarr and Sonarr instance, with whether it answers, how many titles it holds, how many of its root folders are mapped to a category and when it was last synced. Error comes with the reason the instance does not answer, and an instance with no mapped folder routes nothing. Manage opens Instances to change them.
HelpCardFolderMappings: Every root folder the instances report and every destination you declared, with its free space and its state. Pick a category in the Category column and press Save on that row to map it. The form under the table adds a destination folder for an instance, checked against that instance.
HelpCardFolderSuggestions: When the last part of a folder's path names what it holds, as /movies/anime or /tv/kids, Routarr suggests its category: one you made with that name first, then the category of the matching rule template. Map one row, or every row with Map all. A mapped row offers Undo, and the template's rules while you have none of them. Dismiss hides a suggestion for good, and the button under the list shows the dismissed ones again. Nothing reaches Radarr or Sonarr.
HelpCardGuideRestart: On the General tab. Show the guide brings the Getting started steps back on the dashboard and takes you there.
HelpCardGuideTitle: The setup steps from a fresh install to the first moves: connect an instance, map root folders to categories, choose metadata sources, add a rule, run a simulation and turn off the global dry-run. Each step ticks itself once done and its button opens the screen that does it, while steps marked Optional do not count in the progress. Skip the guide folds it to one line, and Show the guide on the General tab of Settings brings it back.
HelpCardDiagnosticsMetadataSources: Every metadata source in the order the rules read them, with its state as the check found it: Connected, active, needs an API key, or Error. Radarr / Sonarr reads active, since the instances above are checked on their own. The line below counts the cached entries and the titles with missing metadata, and says whether the database answers.
HelpCardLibraryFacets: What the library holds for each question a rule can ask: genres, original languages, origin countries, certifications, Arr tags, series types and root folders, each value with how many titles carry it. Check it before writing a condition, since a value the library does not carry matches nothing. A warning above the values counts titles with neither a genre nor an original language, which no metadata condition can see.
HelpCardMetadataTitle: What the metadata sources say about this title: genres, original language, origin countries, certification, keywords, status and synopsis. The sources line names every source that contributed, in priority order, and the status and the synopsis each name their source. When no source has answered, a warning stands in its place.
HelpCardNotificationTest: On the Notifications tab. Sends a message to the saved address in the saved format, signed like the others, so save a change before testing it. The result says whether the receiver accepted it.
HelpCardPreviewTitle: What the rule being edited would change in the library, with nothing saved yet. It counts the titles changing category and how the moves required and the unclassified titles would change, then lists titles that change with their category before and after. Issues with the rule are shown above the figures.
HelpCardRoutarrApiKey: On the Security tab, the key scripts and monitoring send as X-Api-Key. Create or Regenerate it, confirm it is you when asked, and copy it at once: it is shown once. When ROUTARR_API_KEY sets the key, it cannot be changed here.
HelpCardRuleEvaluation: Every enabled rule that applies to this title's media type and instance, in the order the engine reads them, with its priority, its category and its outcome: winner, excluded, matched with lower priority, or did not match. Under each rule, every condition shows whether it held, what it expected and what the title carries. An exclusion that vetoed a rule is named under it.
HelpCardSessions: Each browser signed in, with when its session opened, was last used and ends. End one left open on a shared machine, or Sign out everywhere. Ending the one marked This browser signs you out.
HelpCardSettingsMetadataCoverage: What the sources are asked and how long their answers stay: the titles AniList and MyAnimeList are searched for, the OMDb requests a day, the cache lifetime and the certification regions. A change waits in the save bar until you press Save.
HelpCardSettingsMetadataSources: The sources Routarr asks, split into Active, in priority order and Inactive. Move a source up or down, enable or disable it, and paste the API key of TMDB, OMDb or TheTVDB, or the client ID of MyAnimeList, in its row. Radarr / Sonarr cannot be disabled, only moved, and Save writes the order and the keys together.
HelpCardSettingsTabAutomation: Background sync, Simulate after each sync, Automatic application and the Scheduler tick. With global dry-run off and automatic application on, a warning says that decisions for titles with no files are written without confirmation.
HelpCardSettingsTabGeneral: The Language of the interface and of the messages Routarr writes, and the Theme. A language not fully translated shows its percentage, and Automatic follows the operating system.
HelpCardSettingsTabGuardrails: Global dry-run, Default category, Batch limit and Confirmation threshold. While global dry-run is on, nothing is written to Radarr or Sonarr. Turning it off shows a warning above the tabs.
HelpCardSettingsTabMaintenance: Scheduled backups, their interval and how many are kept, and how long decisions and the move log are retained. Export configuration and Import configuration copy the setup without the Arr API keys, and Purge now removes what is past retention.
HelpCardSettingsTabNotifications: The Notification webhook address, its format and the extra events to send: Failed syncs, Finished simulations and Finished moves. The address is stored encrypted and never exported, and removing it turns notifications off.
HelpCardSettingsTabSecurity: How many days the security log keeps its events, 0 keeping them all. The link under it opens the security log, which lists sign-ins, key changes and refusals.
HelpCardSourceCreditsTitle: The credit each source's terms ask for, with a link to its site. Every source Routarr can ask over the network is credited, enabled or not.
HelpCardSourceRefreshTitle: A Read again button for each saved source Routarr asks over the network. Use it after a source has corrected its data, instead of waiting for the cache lifetime to pass. The result counts the answers read again and those that failed.
HelpCardWebhookSigning: On the Notifications tab. Generate a signing secret so the receiver can check each notification came from Routarr, and copy it at once: it is shown once. Replacing it keeps the old secret signing beside the new one for a day.
HelpFixApiReference1: Make a key on the Applications screen and send it in the X-Api-Key header. It is shown once, so a lost key is replaced by a new one.
HelpFixApiReference2: The badge on the operation names the scope. Scopes are set when a key is made, so create a key that allows it on Applications and revoke the old one.
HelpFixApiReference3: Send the name it gives in confirm back in your request's confirm list. When answerable is false the key may not answer it: make a key that may on Applications, or apply from Routarr's Simulation screen.
HelpFixApiReference4: The search reads the path, the method and the one-line summary, not the descriptions. Try a word of the path, such as decisions or rules.
HelpFixApplications1: A key is shown once and cannot be read again. Create a new key with the same rights, then revoke the old one.
HelpFixApplications2: A key outlives the session that makes it. Type the current password or API key, or sign in again at your provider when your sign-in is older than ten minutes.
HelpFixApplications3: A key's scopes cannot be changed: create a key that allows the scope named in the refusal, which the security log also records, then revoke the old one.
HelpFixApplications4: The question is left to a person: apply those decisions from the Simulation screen, or create a key allowed to answer that guardrail.
HelpFixHistory1: A run records no decision for a title already in its right folder, and the list hides decisions a newer run replaced unless you check "Include decisions replaced by a newer run". To see where any title goes and why, find it on Library and press "Why?".
HelpFixHistory2: The message is the reason Radarr, Sonarr or Routarr gave. Fix what it names, then run a simulation and apply the move again on the Simulation screen.
HelpFixHistory3: Only the latest applied move of a title can be reverted, and only while the title is still in the folder that move put it in and the folder it came from is still a root folder of its instance. Look for the newest Applied row of the same title.

HelpPurposeApiReference: The API reference lists every operation another application may call, such as a script, n8n, Home Assistant or a dashboard, grouped by area, with the scope each needs, its parameters, its responses and a curl example. It is read from the running version, so it matches what this Routarr answers. Make the key on the Applications screen, and download openapi.json for tools that read OpenAPI.
HelpPurposeApplications: Applications gives keys to programs that call Routarr on their own, such as a script, n8n or Home Assistant. Every key can read, and reaches only the scopes, the guardrail answers and the file moves you allow it. Come here to create a key for a new integration, and to revoke one that is unused or has leaked.
HelpPurposeHistory: History lists every decision Routarr recorded: the category and target root folder a run chose for each title, the rule behind it, its confidence and what became of it. Come here to see why a title went where it did, to find a move that failed, or to put an applied move back with Revert. Search a title, filter by status, and include the decisions a newer run replaced when you need them.
HelpPurposeDashboard: The Dashboard sums up what Routarr knows about your library and what it is waiting to do. On a fresh install it holds the Getting started guide, which leads you through setup one step at a time. Later, come here to see how many decisions are pending, whether each instance answers and whether any move failed. Simulation opens the screen where pending decisions are reviewed and applied.
HelpPurposeDiagnostics: Diagnostics checks every Arr instance and metadata source live, and lists every warning that would quietly stop routing: an instance that does not answer, a category with no folder, a missing key, a failed backup. Come here when the navigation shows a warning count or when titles stop moving. Re-check runs every check again.
HelpPurposeInstances: Instances lists the Radarr and Sonarr servers Routarr reads from and writes to. Add one with its address and API key, test the connection, and sync it to read its library and root folders. Come back here to fix an address or a key, to sync on demand, or to copy the webhook address that tells Routarr about a new title right away.
HelpPurposeMoveLog: The move log records every write Routarr made to Radarr and Sonarr: each move an apply sent and each revert, with when it happened, what set it off, the title, the root folders involved and whether it worked. Come here to check what changed in your Arrs, or to read why a move failed. Search by title or details, filter by outcome, and export the matching entries as CSV.
HelpPurposeLibrary: The Library lists every title synced from Radarr and Sonarr, with its instance, its current root folder, the category the last simulation decided and whether metadata is known. Search, filter by type, or tick Unclassified only to find the titles no rule matched. Why? opens the full explanation of where a title goes, where you can ask the sources again or pin the decision as a test.
HelpPurposeMetadataSources: Metadata sources chooses where Routarr reads genres, keywords, countries and ratings for each title, beyond what Radarr and Sonarr report. You order the sources, enable or disable them, give the API keys some of them need, and set how long their answers are kept. Come here when a rule needs data the Arr does not give, such as keywords or origin countries, or when a warning names this screen.
HelpPurposeExceptions: Exceptions force the category of single titles by hand, for the few the rules get wrong. An exception outranks every rule, whatever its priority. Create one with New exception by searching the library and choosing a category, and delete it to hand the title back to the rules. The move itself comes from the next simulation.
HelpPurposeCategories: Categories and folders is where you create the categories your rules route to and map the folders of each instance to them. A title goes to a folder mapped to its category on its own instance, the one with the most room when several share it, so a category with no folder there routes nothing. Come here after the first sync of an instance, and whenever you add a category or a folder.
HelpPurposeRules: Rules decide which category each title belongs to. Each rule holds conditions, optional exclusions and a target category, and rules are read by priority: the first that matches wins. Come here to write rules or start from a template, to reorder, import or export them, and to spot rules that decide nothing. In the editor, Preview impact shows what a rule would change before you save it.
HelpPurposeRuleTests: Rule tests keep the decisions you rely on from changing unnoticed when rules change. Each test is a title pinned with its metadata to the category it must keep landing in. Run tests after editing rules: a failing test says where the title goes now. Pin a test from a title's explanation, opened with Why? in the Library.
HelpPurposeSecurityLog: The security log records every sign-in, every refusal and every change to a key, the password, a backup or the settings, with who asked and from which address. Come here to check who signed in, to spot an address that keeps being refused, or to confirm that a key was made or revoked. Only the owner reads it: no application key can, whatever its scopes.
HelpPurposeSettings: Settings holds how Routarr behaves as a whole, in six tabs: General, Security, Guardrails, Automation, Notifications and Maintenance. Here you set the language, the API key and sessions, the guardrails every apply passes, what runs unattended, where notifications go, and backups and retention. A changed field waits in the save bar, and Save writes every tab together.
HelpPurposeSimulation: The Simulation evaluates every rule against the whole library and lists the resulting decisions, each with the rule that chose it and why, before anything is written. Come here after changing rules or exceptions, or when decisions are waiting for review. Select the moves you agree with and apply them, or apply every move of the run at once with Apply all.
HelpPurposeTasks: Tasks lists every background run with what set it off, its status, its progress and how it ended: syncs, enrichment, simulations, applies, reverts, backups and maintenance. Come here when something seems not to happen, to follow a long apply, or to read why a run failed. A running apply or revert can be stopped with Stop on its row.

RuleAnalysisUnavailable: The rule analysis could not be read, so no badge says which rules decide nothing and the library panel is empty.
RevertAllHint: Moves back every title the filters match whose move can still be reverted, including those beyond this page, in batches.
CategoriesSubtitle: Create the categories your rules route to, and map the folders Radarr and Sonarr know about to them.
RuleAmbiguous: same name and priority as another rule
RuleInstancesHelp: With none ticked, the rule applies to every instance.
RuleImportInstancesMissing: '{name}': limited to instances this installation does not have ({instances}), so it is not imported.
RuleImportInstancesNarrowed: '{name}': limited to the instances this installation has, without {instances}.
RuleImportScopeUnknown: '{name}': imported switched off, as the file does not say which instances it was limited to. Check its instances, then switch it on.
TemplateConcertsDescription: Concert films and stand-up comedy specials, recognised by their TMDB keywords.
TemplateUhdDescription: Films and series of a 4K quality profile, in a library of their own, whatever their genre.
TemplateDocumentariesDescription: Films and series of the Documentary genre.
TemplateChildrenDescription: Family and children's titles, without horror or a rating from 14 years up. It comes before the Anime template, so an anime for all ages goes here.
TemplateAnimeDescription: Series of the Anime type in Sonarr or of the Anime genre, and Japanese animated films.
TemplateForeignDescription: Films whose original language is known and is none of the languages you watch in.
TemplateRequestersDescription: What each person requests through Seerr goes to a category named after them, recognised by the tag Seerr puts on each request.
ErrorTemplateAdded: The template "{template}" has already been added. Replace it, or edit its rules.
ErrorTemplateNoQualityProfile: Choose at least one quality profile.
ErrorTemplateLanguage: "{value}" is not a language Routarr knows. Choose one from the list.
ErrorTemplateQualityProfile: No instance has a quality profile named "{value}". Sync the instance that defines it, then choose it from the list.
TemplatesLead: Ready-made rule sets for the usual library splits. The preview shows what each one would route in your library before anything is saved. Once a template is added, its rules are plain rules, to edit, reorder or delete like any other.
RulesStartLead: No rules yet, so every title goes to the default category. A template adds the rules of a usual split, and its preview shows what they would route in your library before anything is saved.
TemplateNeeds: Source needed, not set up yet: {sources}
TemplateRequestersNone: No title carries a requester tag from Seerr yet. In Seerr (or Overseerr, Jellyseerr), enable Tag Requests in the Radarr and Sonarr settings, then sync the instances.
TemplateRequestersEmpty: No Seerr request found in your library yet.
TemplateRequestersHelp: Each person ticked gets a rule that sends what they asked for to their category.
TemplateRequestersUpdateHelp: People already routed keep their rule as it stands, edits included. Unticking one removes their rule.
TemplateRequestersRemoveQuestion: The rules routing {names} will be removed. Go on?
TemplateCategoryHint: The titles it recognises go to this category, created if it does not exist yet.
TemplateLanguagesHint: A film whose original language is known and is none of these goes to the category.
TemplateQualityProfilesHint: A film or a series of one of these profiles goes to the category, whatever its genre.
TemplateNoQualityProfile: No quality profile is known yet. Sync an instance, then come back to choose its 4K profiles.
TemplateQualityProfilesEmpty: No quality profile reads as 4K yet: choose yours when adding it.
TemplateCreates: The category "{category}" will be created. It has no folder yet, so its titles will not be moved until you map it to one.
TemplatePreviewing: Working out what it would do…
TemplateReplaceQuestion: Replace the rules the template "{template}" added? Changes you made to them are lost.
TemplateCreatedUnmapped: The category "{category}" has no folder yet. Map it to one on Categories and folders, or its titles will not be moved.
TemplateReachCaption: Titles it recognises in your library
TemplateReachNone: It recognises no title in your library yet.
TemplateTakenHint: For the template to decide them, place its rules above yours once added.
TemplateNothingMoves: Adding it moves nothing: titles move when a simulation is applied.
TemplateKeptBy: Kept by your rules placed before
HelpCardTemplates: Ready-made rule sets for the usual library splits: children and family, anime, documentaries, concerts and stand-up, foreign-language films, and Seerr requests by person. Before you add one, the preview shows what it would route in your library. Its rules go after the ones you wrote, and you edit or delete them like any other.
HelpCardTemplateEffect: What adding the template would do, with nothing saved yet: how many titles of your library it recognises, how many would move, are already in place or wait for a folder, and the rules in place that would keep some of them. Nothing moves until a simulation is applied.
RuleShadowedHint: Items matched and never won: {count}. "{rule}" takes them first.
RuleTestNameTooLong: The test name is too long. Maximum characters: {max}
RuleTestsFailed: Tests no longer routing where they were pinned: {failed} of {total}.
RuleTestsPassed: All tests still route where they were pinned. Checked: {total}.
RuleTestsSubtitle: Pinned decisions, replayed against the rules as they stand. The preview says what a change would do. These say what it must not do.
RulesSubtitle: Priority-ordered conditions that classify media into target categories. The first matching rule wins.
SaveHeldInvalid: Save waits for every marked value to be within its bounds.
SecretConfiguredPlaceholder: A key is stored. Type to replace it
SecretStoredPlaceholder: A value is stored. Type to replace it
SectionHasInvalid: {section}: a value is outside its bounds
SettingAnimeSearchHelp: AniList and MyAnimeList list anime alone. Animated titles are the ones Radarr or Sonarr file under Animation or Anime, anime series, and titles with no genre yet. Every title asks them about live action too, which takes far longer on a large library.
