CreditTmdb: Routarr uses TMDB and the TMDB APIs but is not endorsed, certified, or otherwise approved by TMDB.
CreditTvdb: Metadata provided by TheTVDB. Please consider adding missing information or subscribing.
CreditOmdb: Data from OMDb, licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0.
CreditTenrai: Data from MyAnimeList, read through Tenrai.
SettingAutoApplyHelp: Applies a routing decision as soon as it is made, without waiting for a click, but only for media that have no files yet, so nothing is ever moved on disk. Global dry-run still overrides everything, and nothing is applied while a rule test fails. An instance can be kept to proposals from its settings on Instances.
SettingAutoSimulateHelp: Keeps the pending decision list current without running a simulation by hand.
SettingAutoSyncHelp: Poll each instance on its own interval.
SettingBackupEnabledHelp: Take one automatically, on the interval below.
SettingBackupIntervalHelp: How long between two scheduled backups.
SettingBackupRetentionHelp: Past this count, the oldest is deleted.
SettingBatchLimitHelp: Hard ceiling on how many items a single apply may touch. A whole simulation is applied in slices of this size, and always asks for confirmation first.
SettingCertificationRegionsHelp: Comma-separated ISO 3166-1 codes, most preferred first (e.g. FR, US). TMDB and TheTVDB give the rating of the first region they know. When several sources rate a title, the first region's rating wins whatever the order of the sources. Radarr rates for the country set in its metadata settings, Sonarr and OMDb for the United States, and MyAnimeList on a scale of its own.
SettingRefusedNoRegion: {field} needs at least one two-letter country code.
SettingRefusedRegion: {field}: '{code}' is not a two-letter country code.
SettingRefusedRegionUnknown: {field}: '{code}' is not an ISO 3166-1 country code.
SettingConfirmationThresholdHelp: Above this many items, applying requires a second, explicit confirmation.
SettingDecisionRetentionHelp: Pending, skipped and failed decisions older than this are purged. A reverted or failed move stays as long as its move log entry. Superseded decisions go at once whatever this says. 0 keeps the rest.
SettingDefaultCategoryHelp: Used when no rule matches a media item.
SettingGlobalDryRunHelp: While on, Routarr refuses every write to Radarr and Sonarr, whatever you click.
SettingLogRetentionHelp: Move log entries and task history older than this are purged. 0 disables the purge.
SettingSecurityLogRetentionHelp: Security log events older than this are purged. 0 keeps every event. The log lines the server writes are not affected.
SettingMetadataProvidersHelp: Priority order, highest first: the first source that has a value wins it, and the ones below fill in what it left empty.
SettingMetadataTtlHelp: How long metadata stays fresh before it is re-fetched. TMDB's answers are kept 180 days at most, as its terms require.
SettingNotificationWebhookHelp: A URL Routarr posts a message to when something fails while nobody is watching: an Arr it can no longer reach, or an automatic apply the Arr refused. Sent once per transition, not on every retry. The format below writes it as Discord, ntfy, Gotify or Apprise read it. Stored encrypted and never exported, since the address alone lets anyone post to the channel. Remove it to turn notifications off.
SettingRefusedAddress: {field} takes an http:// or https:// address.
SettingNotifySyncFailedHelp: Sent to the notification webhook: every failed sync, not only when an instance goes down.
SettingNotifySimulationCompletedHelp: Sent to the notification webhook, with the simulation's id and how many moves it proposes, for another application to review.
SettingNotifyMovesCompletedHelp: Sent to the notification webhook: each apply and each revert, with how many titles moved, failed and were skipped.
WebhookSigningHelp: Signs every notification, as Standard Webhooks specifies, so the receiver can check it came from Routarr.
ConfirmReplaceSigningSecret: Replace the signing secret? The current one keeps signing beside the new one for a day, then stops.
ConfirmStopSigning: Stop signing notifications? A receiver that checks signatures will refuse them.
SettingOmdbKeyHelp: Adds certifications and countries from IMDb data. Stored encrypted. Leave blank to keep the current one, or to fall back to OMDB_API_KEY.
SettingOmdbDailyRequestsHelp: How many requests Routarr sends OMDb in a day (UTC), the enrichment, the lookups and the checks together. A free key allows 1,000. Raise it for a key that allows more.
SettingSchedulerIntervalHelp: How often the scheduler wakes up to check which instances are due.
SettingTmdbKeyHelp: A v3 key or a v4 read access token. Adds keywords and origin countries, which no Arr reports. Stored encrypted. Leave blank to keep the current one, or to fall back to TMDB_API_KEY.
SettingTvdbKeyHelp: Answers for series alone, which Radarr gives no TheTVDB id. Its key is free for a project earning under $50,000 a year that credits TheTVDB, as this screen does. Stored encrypted. Leave blank to keep the current one, or to fall back to TVDB_API_KEY.
SettingTvdbPinHelp: Only a user-supported key needs it. Stored encrypted. Leave blank to keep the current one, or to fall back to TVDB_SUBSCRIBER_PIN.
SettingMyAnimeListKeyHelp: MyAnimeList's own answer, beside Tenrai's reading of it. Its agreement lets nobody share a client ID, so make your own: sign in at myanimelist.net/apiconfig/create, choose the App Type "other", give any redirect URL such as http://localhost/oauth, then copy the client ID here. Stored encrypted. Leave blank to keep the current one, or to fall back to MAL_CLIENT_ID.
SettingsSubtitle: Safety guardrails, scheduling, notifications and retention.
SourcesSubtitle: Where genres, keywords, countries and ratings come from, in the order that settles a disagreement.
SignInRefused: The sign-in did not complete. Try again.
SignInWithProviderHelp: Routarr does not hold your password: your identity provider decides who gets in.
SignInWrongCredentials: The username or the password is wrong.
ErrorSignInHeldBack: Too many failed sign-ins came from this address. Seconds to wait before the next one: {seconds}
ErrorSignInBusy: Too many sign-ins are being checked at once. Try again in a moment.
ErrorSignInAgain: Sign in again at your provider first: making or removing a key needs a sign-in from the last ten minutes.
ErrorProofPasswordWrong: That is not the current password.
ErrorProofKeyWrong: That is not the current API key.
ErrorPasswordTooShort: A password needs at least {min} characters.
SimulationReplaced: A newer simulation replaced these proposals.
SimulationEmptyState: Run a simulation to see what Routarr would do. Nothing is written until you apply.
SimulationSubtitle: Evaluate every rule against the library and review each proposed move, with its justification, before anything is written.
SkippedUnmappedWarning: Items matching a category with no root folder on their instance: {count}. They will be skipped. Map the category on the {screen} screen.
TasksSubtitle: Every background run (sync, enrichment, simulation, apply, revert, backup and housekeeping) with its progress and failures.
Title: Title
UiLanguageHelp: Language of the interface and of the messages Routarr produces.
InternalError: Routarr failed on its side. The server log says why.
Unauthorized: Your sign-in ended, or the key was refused.
DialogLoadFailed: Part of the interface could not be loaded, often after an update. Reload the page to fetch it.
UpstreamHandshakeFailed: The secure connection to {service} failed: its certificate is not trusted, or the address says https for a port that serves plain HTTP.
UpstreamMetadataAddress: A cloud host's metadata service answers at the address of {service}, where Routarr does not connect.
UpstreamNameUnresolved: The host name of {service} does not resolve.
UpstreamNotHttp: What answers at the address of {service} does not speak HTTP: the port may be another service's, or need https.
UpstreamRedirectedTo: {service} redirects to {host}, which Routarr does not follow.
UpstreamRedirectLoop: The address of {service} redirects in a loop.
UpstreamSignInInFront: Something in front of {service} asks for its own sign-in.
UpstreamTooLarge: The answer of {service} is larger than {size}.
UpstreamUnreachable: {service} cannot be reached: the connection was refused, or the host is unreachable.
UpstreamWriteRedirected: {service} redirected a write, which would reach the new address as a read. Give Routarr the address it redirects to.
ValidationCategoryUnmapped: Category '{name}' is not mapped to any root folder, so matching media will be skipped
ValidationConditionEmpty: {condition} has no value and can never match. Pick at least one, or remove it.
ValidationConditionMediaType: {condition} is never known for the titles this rule applies to, so it can never match.
ValidationConditionNoSource: {condition} needs metadata that no enabled source provides
ValidationContradiction: Conditions '{first}' and '{second}' contradict each other and can never both match
ValidationDescriptionTooLong: The description is too long. Maximum characters: {max}
ValidationExclusionConflict: Condition '{kind}' is both required and excluded, so the rule can never fire
ValidationNameTooLong: The rule name is too long. Maximum characters: {max}
ValidationNoConditions: A rule needs at least one condition
ValidationPriorityRange: The priority must be between {min} and {max}.
ValidationValueNotCode: {condition}: '{value}' is not the code the sources write. Use '{code}' instead.
ValidationValueRepeated: {condition}: '{value}' repeats a value already listed. Keep one of them.
ValidationYearImplausible: {condition}: the year {year} is not between {min} and {max}, the range Routarr accepts
ValidationTooManyConditions: A rule holds at most {max} conditions, and as many exclusions.
ValidationValueBelowOne: {condition}: {value} is too low. Use 1 or more.
ValidationYearRangeInverted: {condition}: the year range from {min} to {max} is inverted and will never match
ValidationRuntimeRangeInverted: {condition}: the runtime range from {min} to {max} is inverted and will never match
ValidationRuntimeImplausible: {condition}: the runtime {value} is not between 0 and {max}, the minutes Routarr accepts
ValidationScoreScale: {condition}: "{value}" is not a scale Routarr knows
ValidationScoreImplausible: {condition}: the score {value} is not between 0 and {max}, the range of its scale
ValidationScoreRangeInverted: {condition}: the score range from {min} to {max} is inverted and will never match
ValidationScoreNoVotes: {condition}: {scale} gives no vote count, so a minimum of votes would never match
WarnApiExternalAuth: Authentication is delegated to a reverse proxy: anything reaching this port directly is unauthenticated.
WarnApiUnauthenticated: The API is unauthenticated. Set ROUTARR_AUTH to apikey, forms or oidc to require a sign-in.
WarnOidcOpenToAnyone: Every account the OpenID Connect provider authenticates signs in with full access. Name the people or the groups who may in ROUTARR_OIDC_ALLOWED_SUBJECTS or ROUTARR_OIDC_ALLOWED_GROUPS, and remove ROUTARR_OIDC_ALLOW_ANYONE.
WarnInstanceNoMapping: Instance '{name}' has no root folder mapped to a category.
WarnWebhookNeverDelivered: {instance} has sent Routarr no webhook yet, so a new title waits for the next sync instead of being routed before it downloads. Copy its webhook URL from Instances into Radarr or Sonarr, tick the events listed there, and press Test.
WarnBackupFailed: The last backup failed. The Tasks screen says why.
WarnBackupCopyFailed: The last copy of the backups to {folder} failed. The Backups card, on the Maintenance tab of Settings, says why.
WarnDeprecatedApiCalled: The application key {name} still calls API paths that a release before 1.0 removes: {paths}. Last call on {date}. The API reference screen names the path that replaced each one.
WarnDeprecatedApiCalledPerson: Routarr's own API key or a session still calls API paths that a release before 1.0 removes: {paths}. Last call on {date}. The API reference screen names the path that replaced each one.
WarnBackupOverdue: No backup was taken in twice the interval set. The Tasks screen shows the attempts.
WarnDataDiskLow: The disk holding Routarr's data has {free} left, less than a backup needs. Free some space before the database or a backup fails.
WarnDataDiskLowReplaced: The disk holding Routarr's data has {free} left, less than a backup needs. The database the last restore replaced takes {size} of it: delete it from the Backups card, on the Maintenance tab of Settings, or free some space elsewhere before the database or a backup fails.
WarnRestorePending: The archive {name} is staged, and the next start restores it over the current database, whenever that start comes. Withdraw it from the Backups card, on the Maintenance tab of Settings, if it is no longer wanted.
WarnCertificationCountry: {name} rates titles for {country}, which is not among the certification regions ({regions}). Its ratings count only after those of the regions: add {country} to them on the Metadata sources screen if they should count as much.
WarnCertificationCountryChanged: {name} now rates films for {country}, and the films it rated before keep the previous country's ratings until each is refreshed. Refresh every movie in Radarr, then sync {name} here.
WarnMissingMetadata: Media items with no external metadata yet: {count}.
WarnNoEnabledInstance: No enabled Arr instance, so there is nothing to route.
WarnProviderNeedsKey: {provider} is in the source list but has no API key: what only it provides cannot match.
WarnProviderKeyUnlisted: {provider} has an API key in {variable} but is not in the source list, so it is never asked. Enable it on the {screen} screen, or remove the variable.
WarnProviderUnreachable: {provider} is configured but does not answer.
WarnProviderRateLimited: {provider} asked for fewer requests. Routarr keeps to its pace and asks again later.
WarnProviderKeyRefused: {provider} refused its key. Check it on the Metadata sources screen.
WarnProviderQuota: {provider} has used the requests it may send today. The titles still to enrich are asked after midnight (UTC).
WarnSchedulerPanicked: Unattended background passes that failed in the last 24 hours: {count}. Syncing continued, but check the server log.
WarnSettingAboveMaximum: Setting '{key}' is {value}, above the maximum of {max}. It stays as it is until it is saved lower.
WarnBackupPassphraseUnreadable: The backup passphrase cannot be opened with the master key in place, so no backup is taken. Set the passphrase again in Settings.
WarnUnmappedCategories: Categories not mapped to any root folder: {count}. Matching media will be skipped.
WebhookTokenRotated: Webhook token rotated. Update it in the Arr
WebhookUrlCopied: Webhook URL copied to the clipboard
WebhookUrlCopyFailed: The browser blocked the clipboard. Webhook URL: {url}
WebhookUrlHelp: In {service}: Settings → Connect, add a Webhook with this URL, and under Headers (shown once Show Advanced is on) add X-Routarr-Token with the token below: the token then stays out of the address, which proxies and the Arr log. Radarr 5.16 and Sonarr 4.0.11 and later send headers.
HintMoveLog: Every write to Radarr and Sonarr
HintCategories: Categories and the folders leading to them
HintApplications: Keys for scripts and other applications
CommandPaletteHint: The library is searched by title, and the screens by name.
ErrorTargetUnreachable: '{path}' has not answered for {age}. Applying now may fail.
ErrorTargetNeverReached: '{path}' has never answered. Applying now may fail.
ErrorSourceUnreachable: '{path}', the folder the files are in, has not answered for {age}. Moving them now may fail.
ErrorSourceNeverReached: '{path}', the folder the files are in, has never answered. Moving them now may fail.
ConflictUnreachableFor: Root folder '{path}' has not answered for {age}
DeclareDestinationHelp: A folder the instance can reach, even one it does not list as a root folder. Declare one root folder in Radarr or Sonarr and name the targets beneath it here. The path is checked against that instance, not against this machine.
ApplyReplaced: Replaced since by other moves, not applied: {count}.
ApplyStillMoving: Still moving in the Arr: {count}. The next sync confirms each move.
ApplyStoppedByDryRun: Stopped when the dry-run was turned on: the rest was not attempted.
ApplyStoppedForShutdown: Stopped as Routarr shut down: the rest was not attempted.
ApplyStoppedOnRequest: Stopped on request: the rest was not attempted.
ErrorCapacityUnknown: '{path}' does not report free space, and it sits under no known root folder. {needed} would be moved without anything checking the room.
ErrorDestinationAbsolute: A destination is an absolute path: /data/movies on Linux, D:\Movies or \\server\share on Windows.
ErrorDestinationAlreadyListed: '{path}' is already listed for this instance
ErrorDestinationTwoSlashes: A path opening with two slashes is a share on Windows and a plain folder on Linux. Write a Windows share with backslashes, as \\server\share, and a Linux path with one slash.
ErrorDestinationUnseen: The instance cannot see '{path}'. Check the path as that container sees it.
ErrorDestinationNotOurs: That folder comes from the instance. Remove it there instead
ErrorCategoryIsFallback: The category '{name}' is the one a title no rule matches goes to. Choose another fallback category in Settings before removing it.
ErrorCategoryInUse: The category '{name}' is still in use. Rules: {rules}, root folders: {folders}, exceptions: {overrides}, rule tests: {tests}.
ErrorBodyTooSlow: The request body did not arrive in time. Send it again, or over a faster link.
ErrorBundleVersion: This file is a version {version} bundle, and this Routarr reads version {supported}.
ErrorRuleBundleVersion: This file is a version {version} bundle, and this Routarr reads versions 1 to {last}.
ErrorRuleImportNoneKept: No rule of the file can be imported, so the rules in place are kept. {reasons}
ImportSkippedRuleCategoryRemoved: Rule '{name}': the category '{category}' was removed meanwhile.
ImportRuleAlreadyPresent: '{name}': already in place, so it is not added again.
ImportRulesKept: No rule could be restored, so the rules in place are kept.
ImportSkippedCredential: The setting '{key}' is a credential, which a bundle does not carry. Enter it again.
ImportSkippedSourceKeyless: The source '{source}' has no key here. Enter its key, then enable the source.
ImportSkippedInstanceExists: The instance '{name}' already exists and was left as it is.
ImportSkippedMappingNoCategory: Root folder '{path}' for '{category}' on '{instance}': that category does not exist.
ImportSkippedMappingUnsynced: Root folder '{path}' for '{category}' on '{instance}': sync that instance, then import again.
ImportSkippedDestinationNoInstance: Destination '{path}': no instance here is named '{instance}'.
ImportSkippedRuleTestNoInstance: Rule test '{name}': the instance that held its title is gone from the installation that exported it.
ImportSkippedRuleTestInstance: Rule test '{name}': no instance here is named '{instance}', the one that held its title.
ImportSkippedRuleTestCategory: Rule test '{name}': the category '{category}' it expects does not exist.
ImportSkippedRuleTestUnreadable: Rule test '{name}': the title it pinned cannot be read.
ImportRuleTestAlreadyPresent: Rule test '{name}': already in place, so it is not added again.
ImportSkippedExceptionNotInLibrary: Exception for '{title}' to '{category}': that title is not in the library yet.
ImportSkippedExceptionNotOnInstance: Exception for '{title}' to '{category}': that title is not in the library of '{instance}' yet.
ImportSkippedExceptionNoCategory: Exception for '{title}' to '{category}': that category does not exist.
ImportExceptionOnEveryCopy: Exception for '{title}' to '{category}': the file names no instance, so it is set on every copy of the title. Copies: {copies}.
ErrorBackupRunning: A backup is already running. Try again once it has finished.
ErrorBackupCopyUnset: No copy folder is set: ROUTARR_BACKUP_COPY_DIR is empty.
ErrorBackupCopyNoAnswer: {folder} did not answer. Check that the share is mounted, then try again.
ErrorBackupNoSpace: The disk holding Routarr's data has {free} left, and a backup needs {needed}, so none was written. Free some space, then back up again.
ErrorBackupDownloadProof: A signed-in session downloads an archive once it proves itself again, with POST /api/v1/backups/{name}/download and the current password or API key.
ErrorBackupThisSecond: A backup was taken this second. Try again in a moment.
ErrorBackupFolderHeld: A backup held the backup folder for an hour. Try again later.
ErrorRestoreStaging: A restore is already being prepared. Wait for it to finish.
ErrorBackupUnreadable: This archive cannot be read. It is damaged, or it is not a Routarr backup.
ErrorBackupNoManifest: This archive carries no manifest, so it is not a Routarr backup.
ErrorBackupManifestUnreadable: The manifest of this archive cannot be read. The archive is damaged.
ErrorBackupNotSealed: This archive is named as encrypted and is not, so it is not restored.
ErrorBackupBefore015: This backup comes from Routarr {version}, older than 0.1.5. Restore it with Routarr 0.1.5 first, then take a new backup there and restore that one.
ErrorBackupNewerSchema: This backup comes from a newer Routarr (schema {schema}). Upgrade Routarr, then restore it.
ErrorBackupCannotRestore: The database in this archive cannot be restored: {reason}
ErrorBackupKeyMissing: This archive lists its master key and does not carry it.
ErrorBackupDamaged: The archive is damaged: {entry} cannot be read.
ErrorBackupKeyMismatchVariable: The credentials in this archive cannot be opened with ROUTARR_SECRET_KEY, which the next start uses instead of the archive's routarr.key. Set ROUTARR_SECRET_KEY to the key the archive was taken with, or unset it, then restore again.
ErrorBackupKeyMismatchFile: The credentials in this archive cannot be opened with the routarr.key the next start would use. Set ROUTARR_SECRET_KEY to the key the archive was taken with, then restore again.
ErrorBackupSealedUnknown: This encrypted archive is not one this version of Routarr can read.
ErrorBackupSealedCost: This encrypted archive asks for more memory or time to open than a restore allows.
ErrorBackupSealedDamaged: This encrypted archive is damaged and cannot be opened.
RuleTestSnapshotUnreadable: The title saved with this test can no longer be read. Delete the test and pin it again.
RuleTestInstantUnreadable: The date saved with this test can no longer be read. Delete the test and pin it again.
ErrorCategoryAlreadyMapped: Category '{category}' already leads to '{path}' on this instance. Add this folder to its folders to share its new titles, or choose another category.
FolderSuggestionMain: Named for the whole library: the titles no rule claims go to {category}.
FolderSuggestionAmbiguous: The folder name says several categories: pick the one it holds.
FolderSuggestionShared: Another folder of {instance} says {category} too: pick the one the titles of {category} go to.
FolderSuggestionsLead: Routarr reads the last part of each unmapped folder's path and suggests the category it names. Nothing is mapped until you say so, and nothing is written to Radarr or Sonarr.
FolderSuggestionsPartly: Folders mapped: {count}. These could not be:
ConfirmStopTask: Stop this task before its next move? What already reached Radarr or Sonarr stays done, and the rest is left as it was.
ErrorDestinationNotPlain: Write the folder without "..", "." or an empty segment: {path}
ErrorInstanceNameTaken: An instance is already named {name}. Give this one another name.
ErrorInstanceSyncing: This instance is being synced. Delete it once the sync has finished.
ErrorMoveNotMade: {arr} holds the title in {path}: the move was not made, or was undone.
ErrorMoveUndone: {arr} put the title back in {path}: its files could not be moved.
ErrorMoveSourceUnseen: {arr} cannot see {path}, the folder the files are in. Nothing was moved.
ErrorMoveInstanceRemoved: {arr} was removed from Routarr before the move was confirmed.
ErrorNotEnoughSpaceShared: {paths} sit on one volume: together they would receive {needed}, and it reports {free} free.
SigningSecretUnreadable: The signing secret cannot be opened with this installation's key, so no notification is sent. Replace the secret.
SigningSecretMintedOnce: Copy it now. It is shown once and cannot be read again.
ErrorPreviewsWaiting: Previews are already waiting for the library. Try again once one has finished.
ErrorProposalsReplaced: A newer simulation replaced these decisions with other moves. Review the latest simulation and apply again.
ErrorPurgeRunning: A purge is already running. Try again once it has finished.
ErrorTaskNotCancellable: This task can no longer be stopped: it has ended, or it is not an apply or a revert.
JobDetailAppliedBatchesMoving: Applied: {applied}, failed: {failed}, still moving: {moving}, batches run: {run} of {planned}
JobDetailCancelled: Stopped on request. Done: {done}, failed: {failed}, still moving: {moving}. The rest was not attempted.
JobDetailStoppedByDryRun: Stopped when the dry-run was turned on. Done: {done}, failed: {failed}, still moving: {moving}. The rest was not attempted.
JobDetailStoppedForShutdown: Stopped as Routarr shut down. Done: {done}, failed: {failed}, still moving: {moving}. The rest was not attempted.
SettingNotificationFormatHelp: How each notification is written. Automatic recognises a Discord webhook and a topic on ntfy.sh, and sends Routarr's JSON to any other address. Choose ntfy for a topic on your own server, Gotify for its message address with an application token, and Apprise for an Apprise API address. Routarr's JSON carries the event, its severity and its ids for another application.
NotificationTestHelp: Sends a message to the saved address, in the saved format and signed like the others. Save a change before testing it.
NotificationTestSent: The receiver accepted the test notification.
NotificationTestNoAddress: No notification webhook address is saved. Save one, then send the test again.
NotificationTestRefused: The receiver refused the test notification with HTTP {status}. Check the address and the format.
NotificationTestUnreachable: The test notification did not reach the address. Check that it is right and that Routarr can reach it.
NotificationMessageAutoApplyFailed: Routarr could not apply every routing decision automatically. Failed: {failed}, applied: {applied}. First error, on {title}: {error}
NotificationMessageAutoApplyHeld: Routarr held back the automatic moves on {instance}, more than one unattended run may make. Moves waiting: {candidates}, batch limit: {cap}. Apply them from the Simulation screen, or raise the batch limit.
NotificationMessageRuleTestsFailing: Rule tests failing: {failed} of {total}. A rule no longer routes a title where a test expects it, and automatic application waits until they pass.
NotificationMessageBackupFailed: Routarr could not write its scheduled backup: {error}
NotificationMessageSimulationCompleted: Routarr simulated the library. Titles: {total}, moves proposed: {moves}.
NotificationMessageApplyCompleted: Routarr moved titles. Moved: {applied}, still moving: {moving}, failed: {failed}, skipped: {skipped}.
NotificationMessageMovesSettled: Moves whose files were still on their way have settled. Moved: {applied}, failed: {failed}.
NotificationMessageRevertCompleted: Routarr moved titles back. Moved back: {applied}, still moving: {moving}, failed: {failed}, skipped: {skipped}.
NotificationMessageTest: Routarr reaches this address. Its notifications arrive here like this one.
RadarrBelowVersion: Radarr {version} is older than {minimum}, the oldest release Routarr supports in full: a film it adds is routed at the next sync, not before it downloads.
RequestedHint: The Arr is moving the files. The next sync confirms the move.
SonarrBelowVersion: Sonarr {version} is older than {minimum}, the oldest release Routarr supports in full: a series it adds is routed at the next sync, not before it downloads, and its original language is unknown.
TaskStopRequested: Stop requested: the task ends before its next move.
TermTextApplicationKey: A key made on the Applications screen for one program, such as a script or Home Assistant, sent as X-Api-Key. It reaches only what its scopes allow, is shown once when created, cannot be edited, and stops working at once when revoked.
TermTextApply: Carrying out decisions: Routarr asks Radarr or Sonarr to change each title's root folder, one title at a time, and to move its files on disk too if you tick that box. Every apply passes the guardrails first, and each write is recorded in the move log.
TermTextArrApiKey: The key Radarr or Sonarr shows under Settings, General, Security. Routarr stores it encrypted and sends it only to the address it was saved with.
TermTextAutoApply: Applies a decision as soon as it is made, without a click, but only for titles with no files yet, so nothing moves on disk. Global dry-run still blocks it, and an instance can be kept to proposals.
TermTextBackup: An archive of the database, the master key and the API key, kept beside the database. Without a passphrase it is as sensitive as the key itself.
TermTextBaseUrl: The address Routarr reaches the instance at, with the port and the URL base if the Arr has one. In Docker, localhost is Routarr's own container, so use the Arr's container name or the host's IP address.
TermTextBatchLimit: The most items a single apply may touch. A whole simulation is applied in slices of this size, after a confirmation.
TermTextCachedEntries: Answers from the metadata sources that Routarr keeps, so the sources are not asked the same question again and again.
TermTextCategory: A named destination that rules and exceptions send titles to, such as anime or kids. Names are lower-cased, and a category leads to a folder only through a folder mapping on each instance.
TermTextCertificationRegions: Country codes, most preferred first, such as FR, US. When several sources rate a title, the rating of the first region wins whatever the order of the sources.
TermTextCondition: One test a rule makes on a title, such as its genre, original language or current root folder. The rule's logic says whether ALL conditions must hold or ANY one is enough.
TermTextConfidence: How strongly the winning rule's conditions agree, as a percentage: more conditions that hold raise it, and a rule needing ALL conditions starts higher than one needing ANY. An exception scores in full, a title no rule matched scores zero, and no setting acts on it.
TermTextConfirmationThreshold: Above this many items, an apply asks for a second, explicit confirmation.
TermTextDecision: What one run of the rules chose for one title: its category, the root folder that category leads to on its instance, the rule behind it and why. A decision that moves a title stays Pending until you apply it, which makes it Applied or Failed.
TermTextDefaultCategory: The category a title gets when no rule matches it, shown as default category in the Rule column. It is chosen on the Guardrails tab of Settings, and cannot be deleted while it is the default.
TermTextDestination: A folder you declare for an instance although the Arr does not list it as a root folder, usually one beneath a root folder. Only a declared destination can be removed, on Categories and folders.
TermTextDryRun: While it is on, Routarr refuses every write to Radarr and Sonarr, whatever you click, and simulations still run so you can review their decisions. A new install starts with it on, and it is turned off on the Guardrails tab of Settings.
TermTextEnrichment: Asks the metadata sources about the titles a sync brought in, at the pace each source allows. It runs after every sync, and the rules read what it found.
TermTextException: A category you force on one title by hand. It outranks every rule whatever their priority, and holds until you delete it.
TermTextExclusion: A condition that vetoes its rule: when it holds, the rule does not decide for that title and the next rule is read. The rule list shows exclusions after the word except.
TermTextFailedDecisions: Titles whose latest move failed and that no run has looked at since. The next simulation settles each one, with a new decision or by finding the title already in place.
TermTextFolderMapping: The link between one folder of an instance and a category. A category may lead to several folders of an instance: a title in any of them stays, and a new one goes to the one with the most room. A folder with no category shows (unmapped).
TermTextGuardrails: The checks every apply passes before Routarr writes to an Arr: the global dry-run, the batch limit, the confirmation threshold, and whether the destination answers and has room. Some refuse and some ask you first, and the ones you can set are on the Guardrails tab of Settings.
TermTextInaccessible: The instance could not reach the folder at its last look, as when a NAS sleeps. The mapping stays, and an apply asks before writing there.
TermTextInactiveSource: A source in the active list that has no API key yet. It answers nothing until its key is saved.
TermTextInstance: A Radarr or Sonarr server Routarr connects to with its address and API key. Routarr reads its library and root folders, and writes to it only when a decision is applied or reverted.
TermTextInstanceEnabled: Only an enabled instance is synced and routed. A disabled one keeps its settings, and nothing is written to it.
TermTextLastSync: When Routarr last read the instance's titles and root folders. Never means it has not been read yet.
TermTextMaintenance: Removes the decisions, move log entries, tasks and security events older than the retention set in Settings, and clears data nothing uses any more.
TermTextMappedFolders: How many of the instance's root folders lead to a category. With none, its titles have nowhere to go.
TermTextMayConfirm: The guardrail questions this key may answer on its own: applying a whole simulation, more moves than the confirmation threshold, too little room, or a destination not answering. A question it may not answer is left to a person.
TermTextMetadataCache: How many days an answer stays fresh before the source is asked again. TMDB's answers are kept 180 days at most, as its terms require.
TermTextMetadataSource: A service Routarr asks for a title's genres, keywords, countries, ratings and languages. Radarr and Sonarr's own data is always read, and TMDB, OMDb, TheTVDB, AniList, Tenrai (MyAnimeList) and MyAnimeList itself are added on Metadata sources, in the order you set.
TermTextMissingMetadata: Titles nothing is known about yet: no genres from their Arr and no answer from any source. Rules on genres, keywords or countries cannot match them.
TermTextMove: An apply changed the title's root folder in its Arr. Details shows the folder it left and the folder it went to.
TermTextMoveFiles: Whether the key may ask an apply or a revert to move files on disk. Without it, such a request is refused.
TermTextMoveLog: The record of every write to Radarr or Sonarr, one line per title moved or put back. A simulation writes nothing to an Arr and adds no line, and nothing is written while dry-run is on.
TermTextNoKey: Marks an operation that needs no key at all, such as /ping, which answers whether Routarr is up for an uptime monitor.
TermTextOperation: One method and path, such as GET /decisions, with what it does. Open it to see its parameters, its request body, its responses and an example.
TermTextOtherSite: A write sent from a page of another site, or a request sent to a host name this Routarr does not answer to, refused. Behind a reverse proxy, your own writes are refused this way when the proxy does not forward the public host.
TermTextOutcome: Success when the Arr took the write. Failure when it refused it, could not be reached or did not finish moving the files, with the reason in red in Details.
TermTextPerformedBy: Who asked for the write: the person the sign-in mode names, or the name of the application key that asked. It is empty when nobody asked or the mode names nobody.
TermTextPriority: The order rules are read in, lower numbers first. The first rule that matches wins, so a broad rule placed above a narrow one takes its titles.
TermTextProof: The password or the API key Routarr asks for again before a key is made or removed. A refused proof is a session that tried without it.
TermTextProposedCategory: The category the last simulation decided for a title. It reads not evaluated until a simulation has read the title, and a lock marks a category forced by an exception.
TermTextRefused: Routarr turned the request away: a wrong password, a key that opens nothing, a scope the key lacks, or a write from another site. Allowed rows are the sign-ins and changes that went through.
TermTextRepeated: Refusals anyone can send fast, such as a key that opens nothing or a write from another site, are written once a minute per address, with how many more came in that minute.
TermTextRequested: The move was sent with its files, and Radarr or Sonarr was still moving them when the apply stopped waiting. The next sync of the instance marks it Applied, or Failed if the Arr did not finish.
TermTextRevert: Moves an applied title back to the root folder it came from, and its files on disk too only if you tick that box. A reverted decision reads Skipped, marked reverted, and the move log records the revert.
TermTextRootFolder: A top folder Radarr or Sonarr stores titles under, as the Arr reports it. Each can be mapped to a category on Categories and folders, and Routarr moves a title by changing its root folder in the Arr.
TermTextRoutarrApiKey: The owner's key, which reaches everything, sent as X-Api-Key by scripts and monitoring. It is shown once when created or regenerated and cannot be read again.
TermTextRule: A set of conditions with a target category. Rules are read by priority, and the first that matches decides where the title goes.
TermTextRuleScope: What a rule applies to: movies, series or both, and the instances it is kept to. With no instance ticked, it applies to every instance.
TermTextRuleTest: A decision pinned as a test: a copy of one title and its metadata, with the category it must keep. Running the tests replays each copy against the rules as they stand, leaving exceptions out. They also run after each sync, and automatic application waits while one fails.
TermTextScheduler: Appears only when an unattended background pass stopped on an internal error. Syncing carries on, its detail names the cause, and the server log says more.
TermTextSchema: The named shape of what an operation takes or returns. A name shown beside a request body or a response is described in the Schemas card.
TermTextScope: What an application key may do, listed under Allows and shown as a badge on each operation of the API reference. Read is always held, and Operate, Write and Configure are granted one by one when the key is made.
TermTextFolderSuggestion: A category Routarr proposes for a root folder no category leads to, read from the last part of its path. It is mapped only when you accept it.
TermTextScopeConfigure: Create, change or remove rules, categories, folder mappings, declared destinations and rule tests: what decides where every title goes.
TermTextScopeOperate: Sync, simulate, apply, revert, run the rule tests and take a backup. Only a key that operates may answer guardrails or move files.
TermTextScopeRead: Everything the screens show, except the settings, the keys and the backup archives. Every key holds it.
TermTextScopeWrite: Add or remove an exception, which forces a title's category.
TermTextSecurityEvent: The kind of thing that happened, such as Sign-in, API key, Application key or Settings. The Details column says what happened in a sentence.
TermTextSimulation: A pass that evaluates every rule against the whole library and records where each title belongs, writing nothing to Radarr or Sonarr. A Preview task is one an application asked for, which stores nothing either.
TermTextSourceApiKey: TMDB, OMDb, TheTVDB and MyAnimeList need a key of your own, pasted in the source's row or set in the environment variable the field names. It is stored encrypted, and a blank field keeps the stored key.
TermTextSourcePriority: The order of the active sources, highest first. The first source that has a value wins it, and the sources below fill in what it left empty.
TermTextSuperseded: A pending decision that a newer run replaced for the same title. It can no longer be applied, so the list hides it unless "Include decisions replaced by a newer run" is checked.
TermTextSync: Reading an instance's library and root folders into Routarr. It runs on each instance's own interval while Background sync is on, and on demand with Sync now or Sync all.
TermTextTask: One piece of background work, recorded from start to finish, with what it did in the Detail column. Its status is Running, Success, Failed, or Stopped when somebody stopped an apply or a revert.
TermTextTrigger: What set a task or a write off: Manual for a person in Routarr, Schedule for the background scheduler, Webhook for a notification from Radarr or Sonarr, Application for an application key, and Automatic for the work that follows a sync.
TermTextWebhook: An address Radarr or Sonarr calls when a title is added, imported, renamed or deleted. Routarr then decides where a new title goes right away instead of at the next sync.
TermTextWebhookToken: The secret that proves a webhook call comes from this instance, sent in the X-Routarr-Token header or inside the URL for an older Arr. Rotating it stops the Arr's webhook until the new value is pasted there.
WarnAutoApplyHeld: Automatic application is holding back the moves on {instance}, more than the batch limit of {limit} allows in one unattended run. Moves waiting: {count}. Apply them from the Simulation screen, or raise the batch limit.
WarnRuleTestsFailing: Rule tests failing: {failed} of {total}. A rule no longer routes a title where a test expects it.
WarnRuleTestsFailingHeld: Rule tests failing: {failed} of {total}. Automatic application waits until they pass.
WarnRadarrBelowVersion: {name} runs Radarr {version}, older than {minimum}, the oldest release Routarr supports in full: a film it adds is routed at the next sync, not before it downloads.
WarnSonarrBelowVersion: {name} runs Sonarr {version}, older than {minimum}, the oldest release Routarr supports in full: a series it adds is routed at the next sync, not before it downloads, and its original language is unknown.
WebhookCheckOk: The webhook in {instance} sends every event Routarr acts on.
WebhookCheckAbsent: No webhook in {instance} points at Routarr yet.
WebhookCheckOtherInstance: The webhook in {instance} points at {other}, another instance: copy this instance's webhook URL from Instances instead.
WebhookCheckTokenStale: The webhook in {instance} sends an old token, which Routarr refuses: copy the token or the webhook URL from Instances again.
WebhookCheckTokenMissing: The webhook in {instance} sends no token, which Routarr refuses: add the X-Routarr-Token header with the token shown in Instances.
WebhookCheckTokenUnchecked: {instance} hides the password its webhook sends, so only a delivery shows whether the token is right.
WebhookCheckMethod: The webhook in {instance} uses {method}, which Routarr refuses: set its method to POST.
WebhookCheckTriggers: The webhook in {instance} leaves {triggers} unticked: tick them, or Routarr hears of those changes only at the next sync.
WebhookCheckTags: The webhook in {instance} is limited to titles tagged {tags}: the others wait for the next sync.
WebhookUrlWithToken: Webhook URL for an older Arr
WebhookUrlWithTokenHelp: Radarr before 5.16 and Sonarr before 4.0.11 add no custom header: keep the address above and enter the token as the connection's Password, with any username. Or paste this address, the token in it. A password stays out of the proxies' logs, but the Arr hides it, so only a delivery shows whether it is right.
RefreshTitleMetadataHint: Reads this title again from every source, and searches AniList and MyAnimeList for it anew.
TitleRefreshedByNone: No source answered. The next pass asks them again.
SourceRefreshHelp: Routarr reads a source's answers again once they are older than the cache lifetime. After a source corrects its data, read its answers again now.
SourceRefreshNone: No source to read again: Radarr and Sonarr's metadata comes with each sync.
TermTextTemplate: A ready-made rule set for a common library split, such as anime or children's titles. Once added, its rules are ordinary rules, and each one records the template it came from.
AuditApplicationKeyExpired: The expired application key {name} ({id}) was sent.
NotificationMessageApplicationKeyExpirin: The application key {name} expires on {date}. Make a new key for its application and revoke this one before then.
ApplicationExpiryHelp: Past this date every call with the key is refused, until you revoke it. Routarr sends a notification a week before. A key is not renewed: make a new one and revoke the old.
JobDetailStoppedArrUnreachable: Stopped: an Arr could not be read for five minutes while it moved files. Done: {done}, failed: {failed}, still moving: {moving}. The rest was not attempted.
JobDetailStoppedArrStalled: Stopped: an Arr has been moving the files of one title for six hours, its queue likely stuck. Done: {done}, failed: {failed}, still moving: {moving}. The rest was not attempted.
JobDetailStoppedSliceRefused: Stopped: the Arr refused every move of a batch. Done: {done}, failed: {failed}, still moving: {moving}. The rest was not attempted.
JobDetailStoppedSliceFailed: Stopped: a batch could not be read from the database. Done: {done}, failed: {failed}, still moving: {moving}. The rest was not attempted.
ApplyStoppedArrUnreachable: Stopped: an Arr could not be read for five minutes while it moved files. The rest was not attempted.
ApplyStoppedArrStalled: Stopped: an Arr has been moving the files of one title for six hours, its queue likely stuck. The rest was not attempted.
ApplyStoppedSliceRefused: Stopped: the Arr refused every move of a batch. The rest was not attempted.
ApplyStoppedSliceFailed: Stopped: a batch could not be read from the database. The rest was not attempted.
ConfirmAddToFolderSet: '{category}' already leads to {folders} on {instance}. Add {folder} to its folders? A title in any of them stays, and a new title goes to the one with the most room.
ErrorDiskFull: The disk holding Routarr's data is full. Free some space, then try again.
ErrorDatabaseBusy: The database is busy with another write. Try again in a moment.
WarnRemovalHeld: {instance} no longer reports {count} titles Routarr holds, more than half of its library. They are kept, with their exceptions, until you remove them from the Instances screen.
RemoveMissing: Remove the titles it no longer reports
ConfirmRemoveMissing: "{name}" no longer reports {count} titles Routarr holds. Sync it and remove them? An exception set on one comes back if the Arr reports the title again.
